Definition: from G1537 and G5594; to expire:--give (yield) up the ghost.
BiblicalUsage: ekpsýchō is the word for give (yield) up the ghost. In Acts 5:5, the text says "and gave up the ghost." In Acts 5:10, the text says "and yielded up the ghost."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading ekpsýchō this way, I believe death is real, but it is not the end — God has the last word over it. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: Ananias and Sapphira; The Death of Herod Agrippa
